limits: Identification rests on two bands (206.5 and 471.5 cm-1) against DFT modes. Many layered compounds could match two bands, so TiNCl is the best-supported candidate, not a confirmed identity. Confidence 0.55 reflects that.
No literature confirmation: the valency search failed (token not set) and the local library has no TiNCl paper. The TiNCl assignment is DFT-based only.
The weak 270.8 cm-1 feature is marginal (about 2.5 sigma) and narrower than the instrument resolution. It is reported as unassigned and should not be used for identification.
The SNR is 17.6 for the strongest band, so weak modes could be missed. The absence of the second strong predicted Ag mode in other candidates is also limited by SNR.
Only the 520.5 cm-1 Si line was detected. The second-order Si features near 950 and 980 cm-1 were not clearly detected in this spectrum.

No polarization data (single spectrum). Irreps are the CRD labels for the DFT structure in backscattering along the layer normal. Whether the measured layer normal matches the crystal axis used in the CRD calculation is not known.

Laser (532 nm) and temperature (295 K) effects on relative intensities and resonance were not assessed. CRD frequencies are DFT (0 K); the 1 to 2 percent scale fit is a per-candidate fit, not a calibration.

Positions are uncorrected. Applying the Si offset of +0.15 cm-1 would move 206.5 to 206.6 and 471.5 to 471.6; this is within the position uncertainties (0.12 to 0.15 cm-1 from the fit, larger after calibration scatter).
No layer number, strain, doping or defect density is claimed; no relation applies to TiNCl in the available reference set.

Rejected: CuPSe3Tl, MgPSe3, AgP2ScSe6 and Al2MgSe4 each have strong predicted modes absent from the spectrum. The graphene, MoS2, WS2, MoSe2, WSe2, hBN, black phosphorus and CrSBr notes were not applicable: their characteristic bands (for example E2g, A1g, G, 2D, or 1366 cm-1) are absent.
